entries.name: Bactrian camel
entries.migrates: nomadic between water and pasture
behaviour: double hump stores fat, not water
can go weeks without drinking, walking to wells on memory
winter and summer coats differ sharply
entries.notes: Wild Bactrians survive only in the Gobi and Taklamakan; the two-humped domestic is the cold desert's pack animal. Camels endure both -40 winters and +45 summers.

entries.name: Gray wolf
entries.migrates: follows prey over wide ranges
behaviour: pack hunts by relay and ambush
trails nomad camps for stock kill
howls coordinate the pack across open country
entries.notes: The wolf is why every wild equid in the biome travels in herds. A recurring menace to camps and herds, not a guaranteed encounter.

entries.name: Przewalski's horse
entries.migrates: nomadic seasonal movements between pasture and water
behaviour: never tamed; the last true wild horse
harem stallion guards mares and foals
stocky with an upright mane and dun coat

voxel_model.pattern: dark dorsal stripe, zebra-like leg barring

entries.notes: Extinct in the wild by the late 1960s, reintroduced in Mongolia's Khustain Nuruu and the Gobi. Critically built for a 'last herd' set piece.

entries.name: Kulan (Asiatic wild ass)
entries.migrates: seasonal, following forage and snow lines
behaviour: forms huge temporary aggregations at water
khulan of the Gobi is a sprint champion
jealously territorial stallions at waterholes

voxel_model.pattern: white belly, dark dorsal stripe

entries.notes: The Gobi's fastest large herbivore after the pronghorn; famous open-dust chase scenes involve wolves behind onagers. Heavily protected.

entries.name: Goitered gazelle
entries.migrates: irregular, following grass and water
behaviour: male larynx swells like a goitre in the rut
lies camouflaged in ditches at midday
large mixed herds in spring, small ones in summer

voxel_model.pattern: white rump, lyre-shaped horns (males only)

entries.notes: The classic Gobi plains gazelle; twins are common in the Dzungarian Gobi. Only males carry horns.

entries.name: Saiga antelope
entries.migrates: massive seasonal migrations, 80-120 km per day
behaviour: trunk-like nose filters dust and chills of -30 winters
whole herds calve within days of each other
irreplaceable: has survived ice-age climate swings

voxel_model.pattern: bulging trunk-like nose, wax-coloured ringed horns (males)

entries.notes: Critically endangered ice-age relic; herds beyond counting gathered in spring are the defining image of the steppe-desert transition.

entries.name: Kiang (Tibetan wild ass)
entries.migrates: follows high-pasture availability; huge herds in winter
behaviour: largest wild ass; blunt muzzle, chestnut coat
territorial bachelor males chase intruders
white belly and leg wedges flash over dark dorsal stripe

voxel_model.pattern: white belly, white wedge behind shoulders, dark dorsal stripe

entries.notes: Lives above 4000 m on the Tibetan Plateau; the biggest wild equid outside Africa. A genuinely exotic spawn for high, cold maps.

entries.name: Argali
entries.migrates: vertical, following snow melt
behaviour: huge spiral horns sweep back over the back
rams butt heads in the rut with audible cracks
light coat flashes against scree

voxel_model.pattern: white rump and belly, dark neck ruff

entries.notes: The snow leopard's main prey; the Altai argali is the largest wild sheep on Earth. Illegal trophy hunting keeps it scarce.

entries.name: Snow leopard
behaviour: rosetted coat vanishes against broken rock
half its body length is tail, used as a counterbalance on cliffs
hauls killed prey home before eating

voxel_model.pattern: dark rosette spots, thick fluffy tail

entries.notes: Ghost of the high desert; an encounter should feel earned. Padding through the Gobi Altai at dusk is the classic set piece.

entries.name: Gobi bear (Mazaalai)
entries.migrates: moves between waterholes and berry plots
behaviour: smallest, most isolated brown bear on Earth
supplemental feeding stations keep it alive
forages sage and wild onion near water
entries.notes: Maybe 30-50 bears left, all in the Great Gobi strictly protected areas of southwest Mongolia. The rarest mammal the game could show.

entries.name: Pronghorn
entries.migrates: some herds migrate 200+ km seasonally
behaviour: fastest land animal in the Americas
white rump patch flares when startled
pronking bounds clear brush

voxel_model.pattern: tan flanks, white rump and black throat bars

entries.notes: Not an antelope at all, but the closest living relative of the North American ice-age speed demons. Iconic of the Great Basin.

entries.name: Mule deer
entries.migrates: elevational, between summer high country and winter desert floors
behaviour: huge ears give it away at dawn
stotting bound with stiff-legged hops
big mule-ish ears and black-tipped tail

voxel_model.pattern: white rump, black-tipped tail, big ears

entries.notes: The deer of the sagebrush; its bounding stot over gullies is unmistakable Looney Tunes motion.

entries.name: Guanaco
entries.migrates: seasonal, following steppe rains
behaviour: stands sentinel while the herd feeds
spits and alarm-calls against foxes
twice the height of a vicuña, and fights harder

voxel_model.pattern: tawny back, white belly and inner legs, grey head

entries.notes: Wild relative of the llama; the base of Patagonia's grazing food pyramid (with puma as its only predator). Wild guanaco is partially tamed as pack stock.

entries.name: Red fox
behaviour: pounces mouse-magnetically from a frozen hover
dens in abandoned burrows and rocks
caches surplus meat in snow

voxel_model.pattern: white-tipped bushy tail, white chin

entries.notes: The everywhere fox; in the cold desert it hunts gerbils and hares along the dune edges and dry washes.

entries.name: Coyote
behaviour: song-dog howls at night, often in trios
adapts to camps and pickings
hunts jackrabbits and rodents by pounce

voxel_model.pattern: brush-black tail bushy, pale muzzle

entries.notes: The Great Basin's balance-keeper; kills pronghorn fawns and eats berries with equal enthusiasm. Fearless of camps but not of guns.

entries.name: Corsac fox
entries.migrates: irregular, tracking rodent plagues
behaviour: hibernates lightly in harsh winters, unlike most foxes
gathers at dens of marmots and ground squirrels
travels wide in bad rodent years

voxel_model.pattern: pale muzzle and bushy tail

entries.notes: Small, sandy and astonishingly cold-adapted; the fox of the classic Gobi badlands shot.

entries.name: Kit fox
behaviour: oversized ears pour off heat by day
lives in dens, often with badgers nearby
sand-coloured soles act as snow shoes

voxel_model.pattern: black-tipped tail, pale cheeks

entries.notes: The little giant-eared shadow of the Great Basin and US southwest; a pup viewed under starlight is unforgettable.

entries.name: Culpeo (Andean fox)
behaviour: biggest fox of South America
pounces on mara pups in the burrows' gardens
cheek-driven trotting along steppe wind

voxel_model.pattern: white-tipped tail, russet nape

entries.notes: Patagonia's fox; the classic 'lone watcher on a rock' at the edge of a mara colony.

entries.name: Tibetan sand fox
behaviour: permanently upturned mouth gives a permanent smile
follows bears digging pikas and snatches escapees
densest coat of any fox, built for 4000 m

voxel_model.pattern: russet crown and back, grey cheeks, white-tipped bushy tail

entries.notes: Iconic plateau fox with a famously smiling face; photogenic at point-blank range, hard to reach at 4500 m.

entries.name: Pallas's cat (Manul)
behaviour: low, broad, flat face with round low-set ears for cold
freezes mid-rock-hop when surprised
sits flat against stone exactly its colour

voxel_model.pattern: dense plush fur, faint barring, white face margins

entries.notes: The angriest-looking small cat alive; a face meme since the internet discovered it at -30 in the Altai.

entries.name: Tarbagan marmot
behaviour: sits bolt upright on hindquarters scanning for eagles
shrill whistle triggers mass retreats into burrows
hibernates six-plus months of the year

voxel_model.pattern: slate-grey and white bands, yellow cheeks

entries.notes: Ground-squirrel sentinel of the Gobi; every pasture has one bolt-upright every hundred metres and they are wildlife-plague sentinels too — flagged for disease risk by nomads.

entries.name: Great gerbil
behaviour: one of the world's greatest rodents by sheer plague numbers
colonies of burrow complexes reshape dunes
digs out underground saxaul forest edges

voxel_model.pattern: sandy back, white belly, long tufted tail

entries.notes: Central Asia's dominant rodent and a plague reservoir; sheer numbers mean a biome can feel like a gerbil world in good seed years.

entries.name: Tolai hare
behaviour: ear tips black, flashes white in alarm
hides in day in a shallow scrape called a form
breeds up to three times a year

voxel_model.pattern: black ear tips, white flanks

entries.notes: The Gobi's hare; a sprint-and-freeze target for the player's bow at dawn.

entries.name: Black-tailed jackrabbit
behaviour: zig-zags at 64 km/h with tail held like a flag
leaps 3 m across sage flats
fans ears for cooling at rest

voxel_model.pattern: black tail, long black-tipped ears

entries.notes: Coyote cuisine given fur; when one flushes from sagebrush, the whole flat changes.

entries.name: Patagonian mara
behaviour: resembles a small-eared hare crossed with a deer
monogamous pairs raise pups in shared burrows
sits on haunches while grazing like a prairie dog on stilts

voxel_model.pattern: orange-tan back, white haunch blaze

entries.notes: Patagonia's oddest rodent; long-lived (~14 years in care) for a rodent, but wild numbers are poorly known. The flagship of the steppe.

entries.name: Golden eagle
entries.migrates: pairs soar year-round on resident territories
behaviour: falconry birds of Kazakh eagle hunters (salburity)
stoops on marmots from 1 km ridge locks
nests on the same cliff ledge for decades

voxel_model.pattern: golden nape, broad dark wings with white base in juveniles

entries.notes: The eagle hunters of western Mongolia fly females on a leather gauntlet; a legitimate 'tamable boss familiar' hook if the design permits.

entries.name: Saker falcon
entries.migrates: many fly to wintering grounds; Gulf falconers trap them
behaviour: the fastest accelerating falcon of the open steppe
stoops onto hares from a mile-high hover
nests on cliffs and abandoned eagle nests

voxel_model.pattern: sandy upperparts, barred cheeks, clean pale moustache

entries.notes: Prized in Gulf falconry and its wild decline is driven by trapping; a natural 'falconry' sky-hunt mechanic candidate.

entries.name: Greater sage-grouse
entries.migrates: seasonal local movements between lek, nest and winter sites
behaviour: males strut on communal leks at dawn, white-breasted balloons
leks return to the same site year after year
cannot digest sagebrush as a chick; insects first

voxel_model.pattern: black belly patch, white breast ruff, spiky tail

entries.notes: The lek is the show: a single arena in an endless sage sea where the game's early explorers could watch half a hundred males strut at dawn.

entries.name: Asian houbara bustard
entries.migrates: migrates between Central Asian breeding grounds and wintering in Gulf
behaviour: exploded lek; males balloon white at dawn
hunted with falcons by Gulf royalty, heavily trapped
walks kilometres for forage, rarely flies

voxel_model.pattern: sandy vermiculated back, white neck plumes, black crest

entries.notes: The reason Gulf falconry exists; its migrations link the Gobi to Arabia. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Darwin's (lesser) rhea
entries.migrates: shifts locally with grazing
behaviour: three toes only; sprints on grass sea
one male incubates a nest of many females' eggs
emptied on the wind, wings spread, faster than puma sprints

voxel_model.pattern: mottled grey-brown, sooty stripes from the neck

entries.notes: Patagonia's ostrich; male-only parenting of a nest of ten to sixty eggs is a superb NPC set piece. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Andean condor
entries.migrates: soars enormous distances between carcasses and roosts
behaviour: wingspan over 3 m; soars without flapping for hours
white ruff and neck wattle mark the adult
roosts socially on cliff ledges facing the wind

voxel_model.pattern: black with white collar ruff and white wing patches

entries.notes: The largest soaring bird on Earth; in Patagonia it hangs on the wind above the steppe and finds the puma's leftovers first. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Burrowing owl
entries.migrates: northern birds migrate; southern are resident
behaviour: lives in burrows dug by prairie dogs and foxes
bobs its head while squeaking like a snake when harassed
decorates its door with dung beetles' remains

voxel_model.pattern: long-legged small owl, white eyebrow stripes

entries.notes: A ten-inch owl that runs its burrow like a pub; loves prairie-dog towns. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Pallas's sandgrouse
entries.migrates: notorious periodic irruptions across western Europe
behaviour: phenomenon flocks that erupt west to Britain in bad years
adult males carry water to chicks in soaking belly feathers
flies 100 km to water several times a day

voxel_model.pattern: black belly patch, barred wings, pin-tailed tail

entries.notes: One of history's great vagrant birds: flocks suddenly appearing over London were the 1863 news of the decade. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Great horned owl
behaviour: the usual nocturnal scream of the American desert
eyelashes of ear-tufts over a cat
kills skunks without blinking; a peerless rodentian assassin

voxel_model.pattern: ear tufts, bright yellow eyes

entries.notes: The owl of every North American ghost story; resident in the Great Basin's basalt rimrock all winter. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Great Basin rattlesnake
entries.migrates: brumates communally in rock dens with hundreds of snakes
behaviour: faded mid-blotched pattern named 'lutosus, the muddy one'
winter dens rattle like maracas in October
if cornered, coils and batters air with a forty-inch body

voxel_model.pattern: buff ground with dark blotches, pale border

entries.notes: A live-bearing cold desert viper; the communal den is a superb hazard set piece — a rock face that hums and shakes in October.

entries.name: Side-blotched lizard
behaviour: rock-paper-scissors throat-colour polymorphism: orange-blue-yellow rock, paper, scissors
lives fast and dies at one year
does dramatic push-ups from sun-warmed stone

voxel_model.pattern: blue-black blotches on sides, barred back

entries.notes: The most studied lizard on Earth for its three-way mating game; an 'invisible detail' that sells believability at your feet.

entries.name: Steppe toad-headed agama
behaviour: flattens like a coin and flares a red tail inside its curled mouth
dances before predators, then plays dead
densest lizard of the Gobi; dozens per hectare on good dunes

voxel_model.pattern: sandy cryptic, black tail-tip flashed red inside gaping mouth

entries.notes: The Gobi's little sphinx; its anti-predator 'come here then drop dead' routine is a delight for attentive players.

entries.name: Camel spider (solifuge)
behaviour: enormous shearing chelicerae, not a spider and no venom
races the shadow line at camp
males carry the female's egg sac to the den
entries.notes: The apocryphal 'wind scorpion' of war reporting; honest in-game they're fast, harmless outside desert shade, and terrifying cargo in horror builds.
